images.caption: Figure 1:Selective 3D modeling.Each method pairs 3D proxy frames with generated video frames at 3, 5, and 7 seconds. Codex + Blender and VideoCoCo explicitly model hands and arms. Coda-DaVinci models the objects involved in cutting and unwrapping, while leaving detailed hand articulation to the video generator.

Figure 2:Qualitative visualization of component configurations.Within each labeled group, the upper sequence shows the proxy
and the lower sequence shows the corresponding generated video;
columns follow the same eight sampled timestamps.
The groups labeledP0andP1correspond toG1_P1_PE1andG0_P1_PE0, respectively.
Both enable explicit physics simulation and differ in geometry
and prompt enhancement.

Figure 5:Overview of Coda-DaVinci.Coda-DaVinci combines task-adaptive proxy construction with proxy-grounded video synthesis. The harness maintains the working scene and supports visual feedback throughout generation.

Figure 6:Performance and ablation studies.(a) Normalized benchmark results.
(b) Ablations of adaptive routing, independent review, and modeling granularity.
(c) Video quality and token cost across rendering engines.
(d) On LongAV-Compass, Coda-DaVinci improves event fulfillment and long-form structure over direct generation, with lower transition stability.
(e) On WBench, it improves interaction adherence and consistency, with lower setting adherence.

Figure 7:Camera instruction following and state persistence.The camera turns away while leaves are being cleared, then returns to the steps. Each method occupies two rows, read consecutively from left to right. Frames are sampled at matching timestamps, with denser sampling during the return. Both code2video methods show cleared steps on revisitation, while Seedance retains substantial leaf coverage.

Figure 8:Hand articulation and visual fluency.Consecutive frames from a dough-flattening task, sampled at 4 fps over 4.50–8.25 seconds. Each method occupies two rows, with the second continuing the first. Compared with the nearly fixed pose of Codex + Blender, Coda-DaVinci shows changing wrist and finger poses through repeated contact with the dough. Seedance provides the direct-generation comparison.

Figure 9:Scene geometry during navigation.R2M-Bench caseWSLRRLL_0046. The portal, curved roof, and surrounding station provide landmarks for comparing scene structure through the camera movement. Proxy renders and generated frames reveal how each modeled scene carries through synthesis.
Figure 10:Scene geometry during navigation (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 11:Preserving an edited scene state.WBench case 248. The monitor goes black before the player stands up and turns around. Direct generation brings back the game display in later turns, while Coda-DaVinci preserves the black-screen state in both the proxy and the generated video.

Figure 12:Scene consistency across successive views.WBench case 92. The camera moves through an autumn park. Coda-DaVinci retains the wooden bench across views; the direct-generation sequence introduces a bench with a different armrest structure. Corresponding proxy frames show the shared scene used for continuation.

Figure 13:Coordinating objects and interactions.VTR-Bench caseCULT-0034. Two friends compare a set of written notes and a tracklist before playing a cassette. Coda-DaVinci represents the tabletop objects and subject identities in the proxy, while the final video supplies natural hand movements and human appearance.
Figure 14:Coordinating objects and interactions (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 15:Preserving task-critical object structure.VTR-Bench caseAD-0059. The task involves adjusting a split keyboard, inspecting its layout diagram, and showing its engraved badge. The proxy specifies the keyboard components and camera views, which guide the corresponding actions in the generated video.
Figure 16:Preserving task-critical object structure (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 17:Following actions within a continuous shot.VTR-Bench caseLIFE-0008. The owner hands over a leash and explains the care instructions before the neighbor hides a key under the frog-shaped planter. Coda-DaVinci keeps these actions within the requested wide view, preserving the room layout throughout.
Figure 18:Following actions within a continuous shot (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 19:Deformation with natural hand motion.T2AV-Compass case0348. The proxy controls the dough flattening beneath the paper doilies. Coda-DaVinci leaves the hands to the video model, producing the requested manipulation around the changing dough shape.
Figure 20:Deformation with natural hand motion (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 21:Natural interaction from a simplified scene.T2AV-Compass case0333. An elderly wheelchair user stops to greet a small dog. The proxy establishes their relative positions and motion, while the generated video supplies the finer posture and appearance of the interaction.
Figure 22:Natural interaction from a simplified scene (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 23:From modeled objects to fine visual detail.T2AV-Compass case0064. The camera approaches a bowl of steaming dumplings in a palace courtyard. Paired proxy and generated frames show how the modeled arrangement is rendered into food texture, pleats, and steam.
Figure 24:From modeled objects to fine visual detail (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.

Figure 25:Subject identity across alternating close-ups.T2AV-Compass case0424. The sequence alternates between a stressed pilot and his focused co-pilot. Coda-DaVinci uses simple subject proxies to establish identity and framing, allowing the video model to generate facial detail and expression.
Figure 26:Subject identity across alternating close-ups (continued).The remaining configurations are shown at the same timestamps, with their corresponding proxy renders.
